documents.unit: AI at Amherst (Academic Technology Services / IT)
documents.title: Updated AI Usage Guidelines
documents.summary: A short college-wide set of AI guidelines, dated January 2026, aimed at the whole community and mostly at staff work. It welcomes exploration of AI while requiring verification, data protection, tool vetting through AskIT and encouraging transparency. It says almost nothing about student coursework or instructor-set course rules.
documents.stance_why: The text says 'We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI' and 'Members of the community may use these tools to generate ideas, drafts, and analyses, provided that' data, verification and standards conditions are met. That is permission with conditions, not an encouragement to adopt AI everywhere, and it does not hand the decision to instructors.

units.why: The College says 'We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI', a welcome of AI use by the whole community, so P02 (permit or encourage by default); modality should because it is encouragement, not a duty.
units.anchor: We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI
units.frag_end: improve how we operate as a community.
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on actor, phase, modality, type and stance. Topics differed: A added learning-rationale; the passage says 'to support learning, spark innovation', so it is added.

units.why: Opening statement that 'generative AI is rapidly reshaping the ways we learn, teach, and work'; it is context for the guidelines, an institution-level framing, so P56 rather than P44 (it does not say courses teach AI use).
units.anchor: generative AI is rapidly reshaping the ways we learn, teach, and work
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. The sentence is the College's own voice ('Amherst College recognizes') stating context, not a duty on a reader, so admin; phase general, informs, P56 agreed.

units.why: The commitment to 'protecting privacy, maintaining accuracy, and upholding the academic and institutional integrity' states the principles the guidelines rest on, an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: protecting privacy, maintaining accuracy, and upholding the academic and institutional integrity
units.resolution_why: Codes agreed (P56, informs). Topics differed: A listed responsible-ai, B integrity-sanctions; the passage names privacy, accuracy and integrity, so privacy-data and integrity-sanctions are kept.

units.why: Scope statement: 'apply to all members of the Amherst community'. It sets who the guidelines cover (P56 framework and scope; P61 is for definitions of AI, which this is not).
units.anchor: These guidelines apply to all members of the Amherst community
units.resolution_why: A coded P61 (scope), B P56. P61 covers definitions of AI that set what a policy covers; this sentence defines no AI term but states who the guidelines cover as part of the preamble. P56 covers 'purpose, scope, and principles', so P56.

units.why: 'Users are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any material they create, distribute, or rely upon' that AI generated or assisted; users own what they produce, which is P29.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any material they create
units.resolution_why: Types agreed (P29). unit_stance differed (A permit, B neutral). The sentence takes no position on whether AI may be used, only on who answers for output, so neutral.

units.why: 'All final decisions, publications, and communications remain the responsibility of the human author or decision-maker' keeps the human as the decision-maker, so P32 (human stays primary) rather than P29, which is about owning submissions.
units.anchor: remain the responsibility of the human author or decision-maker
units.resolution_why: Types agreed (P32). unit_stance A permit, B neutral; the sentence takes no position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: 'Members of the community may use these tools to generate ideas, drafts, and analyses' is a permission for brainstorming and drafting under conditions (the 'provided that' list), so P15; drafting is prose, but the idea-generation use is the main fit.
units.anchor: may use these tools to generate ideas, drafts, and analyses
units.resolution_why: Agreed on P15, may, permit. Anchors differ only in length. Topics: B's writing-assistance kept because 'drafts' is named in the passage.

units.why: First condition of the permission: 'All data used are appropriate for public or internal sharing'; limits what may go into AI tools, so P50.
units.anchor: All data used are appropriate for public or internal sharing

units.why: Second condition: AI-generated material must be 'reviewed and verified by a person before being distributed or published', which requires verification of AI output (P31).
units.anchor: reviewed and verified by a person before being distributed or published
units.resolution_why: Types agreed (P31, must). unit_stance A permit, B restrict; the sentence is a condition limiting the permission ('provided that'), so restrict. Topic set to the existing accountability-understanding tag.

units.why: Third condition: AI use must align with 'academic, professional, and ethical standards, including the Student Code of Conduct'. It binds AI use to existing conduct rules, which no type states exactly (P36 is about classifying misuse as misconduct; P45 about treating AI as a collaborator), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: The use of AI aligns with applicable academic, professional, and ethical standards
units.uncovered_note: AI use must conform to existing college conduct and acceptable-use policies (Student Code of Conduct, Acceptable Use Policy).
units.resolution_why: A coded P45 (existing rules), B UNCOVERED with a note. P45 is about treating AI like a human collaborator or outside source under collaboration rules; the passage only requires AI use to align with 'applicable academic, professional, and ethical standards, including the Student Code of Conduct', with no collaborator analogy. P36 does not fit either since it does not classify misuse as misconduct. Kept UNCOVERED; phase during-work like the other conditions of the permission (A said general).

units.why: 'These resources will be updated as appropriate as guidance changes' says the guidance is provisional and will be revised, so P54.
units.anchor: These resources will be updated as appropriate as guidance changes

units.why: 'Many AI tools do not provide robust privacy or data controls' explains why data must be protected; it is a privacy fact, P50, informs.
units.anchor: Many AI tools do not provide robust privacy or data controls

units.why: 'do not include sensitive, confidential, or personally identifiable information (PII)' in any prompt or upload is a flat ban on entering protected data into AI tools, P50 (protect personal data), unless the licence guarantees no external use.
units.anchor: do not include sensitive, confidential, or personally identifiable information (PII)
units.frag_start: Unless the College’s licensing agreement explicitly

units.why: The examples ('financial, payroll, or donor information; student or personnel records') define what counts as sensitive data under the ban, so a definition inside the privacy rule: P50, informs.
units.anchor: student or personnel records (such as transcripts, evaluations, or tenure materials)
units.resolution_why: A coded must-not/restrict, B informs/neutral. The sentence begins 'Examples include' and illustrates what counts as sensitive under the preceding ban; it states no separate rule, so informs/neutral.

units.why: 'When in doubt, treat all internal information as non-shareable with AI tools unless confirmed otherwise' is a default-deny for unsure cases, but about data; P50 fits better than P10, which is about asking before using AI for coursework.
units.anchor: treat all internal information as non-shareable with AI tools unless confirmed otherwise
units.resolution_why: Both agree on P50, should, restrict.

units.why: Employees 'should consult the College’s Data Classification Policy' to decide what information may be used with AI tools; tells staff where to find the rules, P50.
units.anchor: To determine what information may be used with AI tools, employees should consult the
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. Source: 'employees should consult the College's Data Classification Policy'. A real instruction to staff, kept: P50, ta-staff, should.

units.why: Internal and Shareable data 'should be entered into college-licensed AI tools only', which prefers licensed tools and limits where data goes; P50 (prefer vetted tools), not P17 as no specific tool is provided by this sentence.
units.anchor: should be entered into college-licensed AI tools only
units.resolution_why: A coded must, B should. The source says 'should be entered', so should. Actor ta-staff agreed (section addresses employees).

units.why: Sensitive (Yellow) data 'may be used with college-licensed AI tools following review and approval by AskIT'; a conditional permission with a review gate, P50.
units.anchor: may be used with college-licensed AI tools following review and approval by AskIT
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B permit. The sentence says sensitive data 'may be used ... following review and approval by AskIT': a conditional permission, so permit.

units.why: Before adopting new AI tools or enabling AI features, users must 'consult AskIT to confirm that appropriate privacy, security, and risk assessments have been completed'; a vetting rule (P50 prefer vetted tools), and P07 does not fit as it requires review rather than covering built-in AI by rule.
units.anchor: consult AskIT to confirm that appropriate privacy, security, and risk assessments
units.frag_start: Before adopting new AI tools or
units.resolution_why: Matched; A also wrote a normalized policy, B left it null. The anchor alone states the rule, so null. Agreed on P50, must, before-course, restrict.

units.why: The review requirement 'includes tools or features within commonly used college platforms such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Workday, Slate, and Tableau', i.e. AI embedded in existing platforms: P07.
units.anchor: features within commonly used college platforms such as Google Workspace
units.frag_start: This includes tools or features within
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. Source: 'This includes tools or features within commonly used college platforms such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365...'. A real clause extending the review duty to AI embedded in existing platforms, kept as P07; A folded it into the neighboring vetting unit.

units.why: 'Do not use College data in any manner which may lead to its use in model training' bans a use of data with AI, P50 (privacy); P65 is institutional contract review, not user conduct.
units.anchor: Do not use College data in any manner which may lead to its use

units.why: 'Generative AI systems can be inaccurate, inconsistent, or biased' states why output must be checked: P31 (output is often wrong), informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI systems can be inaccurate, inconsistent, or biased

units.why: 'Always review and fact-check their suggestions, particularly in technical, academic, or policy-related work' directs users to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Always review and fact-check their suggestions
units.resolution_why: Types agreed (P31, must). unit_stance A permit, B neutral; the sentence takes no position on whether AI may be used, so neutral.

units.why: Repeats responsibility but extends it to 'material, code, or workflows' generated or assisted by AI, so it is a distinct statement covering code; P29 (own what you submit/distribute).
units.anchor: accuracy and integrity of any material, code, or workflows they create
units.resolution_why: Agreed P29, must. unit_stance A permit, B neutral; no position on AI use, so neutral. Kept as a separate unit because it adds code and workflows.

units.why: 'transparency is encouraged' when AI plays 'a significant role' in work; a soft disclosure expectation (P24 disclose AI use), modality should since it is only encouraged and limited to significant use.
units.anchor: transparency is encouraged
units.frag_start: When AI tools play a significant
units.resolution_why: A coded one unit for the pair of sentences (anchor on the second sentence, unit_stance permit); B coded two. 'transparency is encouraged' is the rule (soft disclosure, P24, should); unit_stance encourage follows the word 'encouraged'. B's second unit ('Clearly indicating ... supports honesty and trust') only restates the reason in the same passage and was dropped.

units.why: 'For questions about the technical, privacy, or security aspects of AI use, or to request a review of a new AI tool, contact AskIT' names where users go for help and for tool review. It is a procedure for all users, so actor all, may. No type covers support routing; P50 is about data protection and vetted tools, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: or to request a review of a new AI tool, contact
units.uncovered_note: Names a support contact (AskIT) for technical, privacy and security questions and for requesting review of a new AI tool.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. The closing 'Questions and Support' section is a real procedural statement (who to contact), not navigation, so kept. B skipped it; neither coder found a fitting type, so UNCOVERED.

notes: Only one included document; mostly employee-facing, so student-coursework types are absent. One UNCOVERED unit: AI use must align with existing conduct and acceptable-use policies.
